did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens by declaring that the earth, the world, and all its inhabitants belong to the LORD.
Did you know? According to the psalm, the LORD established the earth upon the seas and founded it upon the rivers.
Did you know? The psalm presents two parallel questions: Who may ascend the mountain of the LORD, and who may stand in his holy place?
Did you know? The requirements are clean hands, a pure heart, refraining from lifting up one’s soul to what is false, and not swearing deceitfully.
Did you know? The one who meets these requirements will receive a blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
Did you know? The psalm calls such people “the generation of those who seek him”—those who seek the face of the LORD and are identified with Jacob.
Did you know? As the King of glory enters, the gates are called to lift up their heads and rise, and the ancient doors to open.
Did you know? The King of glory is identified as the LORD, described as “strong and mighty” and “mighty in battle.”
Did you know? The call to the gates is repeated a second time, again emphasizing their rising in preparation for the coming of the King of glory.
Did you know? At the end of the psalm, the King of glory is called “the LORD of hosts,” and the psalm concludes with the emphatic declaration: “He is the King of glory forever.”
